The card background is applied via INLINE style (or a dynamic class that Tailwind isn't compiling), so the .app-shell class-based bg-white/tint override (rule 1 in the CSS layer) does NOT match, but the global text-whitening rule still forces the text white. The chip has bg-* on itself so the ':not([class*="bg-"])' safety guard doesn't help because the text node inherits color from an ancestor rule OR the chip's own text-* class is one of the dark-accent tokens that gets remapped. Occurs on /support for every ticket row.

critical_code_review_comments: The CSS override strategy in /app/frontend/src/index.css (System-wide dark-mode adaptation block) is class-scoped via [class~="..."] whitelists. Any component that sets background via INLINE style with a hex NOT paired with one of the whitelisted accent-border tokens will slip through — which is exactly what happens on ATHM project cards. Consider a follow-up: sweep the codebase for `style={{ backgroundColor: '#E' | '#F' }}` inside pages under /app/frontend/src/pages/**/*.jsx and either replace with a themed class or ensure the sibling accent-border token is present.

Global 'whiten text under .app-shell' rule fights local pill/chip colors. The ':not([class*="bg-"])' guard is on the sect-teal/clay/sage rule but not evenly applied — MySupport status chips prove that. Recommend adding chip-safe carve-outs (e.g. [data-testid^="ticket-status-"]) OR having chips ship explicit text-* classes that survive dark mode.

rca of the issue: The .app-shell dark-mode CSS layer uses class-attribute selectors ([class~='bg-[#HEX]'] and [class~='border-[#HEX]']) to remap light surfaces. It cannot see INLINE background-color styles unless the sibling accent-border-token class is also present. AthmProjects card fills are inline-styled without such a paired token, so the fill stays light while the global text-whitening rule flips the text white → unreadable. MySupport chips carry their own bg-* and text-* classes, but the text-* token happens to be one of the accent tokens that the layer remaps to white ink, and chip bg is a solid light cream/grey that never gets darkened. LettersFollowUps group toggle uses a near-black text token that is not in the whitelisted set, so it stays dark on a dark card — the opposite problem (dark-on-dark).
